title: Seahawks Put Running Back Jadarian Price on Injured Reserve, Impacting 2024 Roster Outlook
body:
Seattle’s coaching staff confirmed on Saturday that running back Jadarian Price has been placed on injured reserve, sidelining him for the upcoming Sunday matchup and at least the following three games. The move caps a brief, injury‑marred stretch for the 24‑year‑old, whose chest injury was diagnosed after a hard hit during practice earlier this week. Seattle will now have to adjust its backfield depth while hoping the young back can recover fully before the season’s second half.

Price, a fourth‑round pick out of Texas A&M, entered the season as a versatile component of the Seahawks’ rushing attack, offering both inside power and the ability to line up in the slot as a receiver. In the first three games of the year, he logged 35 carries for 162 yards and a touchdown, while also catching six passes for 48 yards. Though his numbers were modest, the coaching staff praised his work ethic and his readiness to step in when starter Rashaad Penny was limited by a lingering hamstring issue. The chest contusion, however, forced the team’s medical staff to take a cautious approach, resulting in the IR designation that automatically removes a player from the active roster for a minimum of four weeks.

The Seahawks’ backfield now leans heavily on Penny, who has shown flashes of explosiveness despite his own injury concerns, and rookie running back Tyler Holt, who has been promoted from the practice squad to fill the void. Holt’s recent performances have been encouraging; he recorded 45 rushing yards and a 12‑yard reception in the previous game, suggesting he could handle an expanded role. Nevertheless, analysts note that the loss of Price’s dual‑threat capability may limit Seattle’s play‑calling options, especially in third‑down situations where his pass‑catching skill set has been a valuable asset.

Seattle’s offensive coordinator, Shane Waldron, addressed the situation in a press conference, emphasizing the team’s “next‑man‑up” mentality. “Jadarian’s health is our top priority,” Waldron said. “We’ve got depth at running back, and we’ll adjust our schemes to keep the offense moving. It’s a tough blow, but we’ve dealt with injuries before and we’ll keep pushing forward.” The Seahawks’ medical team indicated that Price’s injury, while painful, does not involve structural damage, and they expect him to begin a gradual rehab program within the next 48 hours. The IR move also frees a roster spot, which Seattle could use to sign a veteran defensive lineman or bolster its special teams unit, areas that have been identified as needing reinforcement.

The broader impact of Price’s absence extends beyond the immediate roster shuffle. Seattle’s upcoming schedule features two consecutive road games against the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Rams, both of which field strong defensive fronts. Without Price’s ability to pick up blitzes and provide a reliable outlet in the passing game, the Seahawks may find it more challenging to sustain drives against those defenses. Moreover, the timing of the injury coincides with a critical stretch of the season where the NFC West race tightens, and every offensive contribution becomes vital for playoff positioning.

Looking ahead, Seattle will monitor Price’s progress closely, with the earliest possible activation date set for Week 7. In the meantime, the team’s focus will be on integrating Holt and other depth players into the offensive rotation, while maintaining a balanced attack that can adapt to the loss of a key piece. If the Seahawks can successfully navigate this setback, they will not only preserve their momentum but also demonstrate the resilience that has defined their campaign thus far. The coming weeks will test the depth of the roster and the coaching staff’s ability to innovate, setting the stage for a pivotal juncture in Seattle’s 2024 season.
